cookieBanner.text: We use Google Analytics to understand how the site is used. It starts only if you accept. If you refuse, the site works the same and nothing from Google is loaded.

privacyModal.title: Privacy notice
privacyModal.subtitle: EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR 2016/679) and new Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP)
privacyModal.calloutDesc: The data you enter in the program does not go to third parties. The site uses Google Analytics only if you accept cookies.
privacyModal.section1Title: Section A: Windows application (local SQLite database)
privacyModal.section1Text: When you use the Windows application on your computer or a USB drive:
section1Bullets: Accounting data: the application does not send any entered data (customers, amounts, invoices, bank accounts) to external servers or to third parties.
Local database: all data is saved only on the user's computer, in an SQLite database. The user is the sole controller of their own business data.
Tracking: no invasive collection of usage data and no tracking of the user's activity.
section2Bullets: Browsing data: the site records normal connection data (anonymised IP address, browser type), used only for security and to prevent abuse.

Cookies: no profiling or advertising cookies. Google Analytics (statistics) starts only if you accept; you can change your choice from “Cookie preferences” at the bottom of the page. Details in the full privacy notice.
Contact: the address info@fatturafacile.eu is used only to reply to technical and administrative requests sent voluntarily.
privacyModal.section3Title: Section C: your rights and the law
privacyModal.section3Text: Under articles 15-22 of the EU GDPR and articles 25-29 of the Swiss nFADP, individuals have full rights of access, rectification, portability and erasure.

faq.searchPlaceholder: Search for an answer (e.g. backup, QR-bill, price)...

items.question: Is it really free?
items.answer: Yes. FatturaFacile is open source software under the MIT licence: you use it for free, with no subscription and no hidden costs. The code is public.

items.question: Where is my data?
items.answer: In the web version it is on the server where the program is installed: if you install it, it is on your server. In the upcoming Windows app it is only on your computer. The demo holds sample data only.

items.question: How do I make a backup?
items.answer: The web version makes an automatic copy every night and keeps the last 7. You can also make one by hand, download it and restore it whenever you want.

items.question: Does it send the invoice straight to the Italian tax system (SdI)?
items.answer: Not yet. FatturaFacile creates the electronic invoice file (FatturaPA, XML format): you download it and upload it to the Fatture e Corrispettivi portal of the Italian Revenue Agency, or give it to your accountant. Direct sending is in development.

items.question: How does it work for Switzerland?
items.answer: The invoice includes the payment slip with QR code (QR-bill), in the format Swiss banks require. It works with QR-IBAN and with a normal IBAN, in Swiss francs or euros, with Swiss VAT rates.

items.question: Can I ask for a feature or help out?
items.answer: Yes. Write to us in the Telegram group or open an issue on GitHub. We are also looking for people to translate, test the program or check the tax rules.

items.question: How do I try it?
items.answer: Open the online demo: it is the real program with sample data, no sign-up. Do not enter real data, because it is erased from time to time.

items.question: Who is it for?
items.answer: For tradespeople, small businesses and freelancers in Italy and Switzerland who make quotes and invoices and do not want to pay a subscription.

section2Bullets.desc: The contact email address (info@fatturafacile.eu) is used only to reply to technical and administrative requests sent voluntarily.

privacy.section2bTitle: Section C: web version and demo
privacy.section2bIntro: When you use the web version of FatturaFacile or the online demo:

section2bBullets.title: Data you enter
section2bBullets.desc: Customers, amounts and invoices are on the server where the program is installed. If you install it yourself, they are on your server and you are the controller. We do not sell them or give them to third parties.

section2bBullets.title: Demo
section2bBullets.desc: In the demo, use sample data only: do not enter real customer or business data.

section2bBullets.title: Backups
section2bBullets.desc: The web version makes an automatic copy every night and keeps the last 7. You can also make one by hand, download it and restore it.

section2bBullets.title: Statistics
section2bBullets.desc: Google Analytics is present only on this information site (fatturafacile.eu), not inside the program.

privacy.sectionGaTitle: Section D: Google Analytics and cookies
privacy.sectionGaIntro: This site uses Google Analytics 4 to understand how it is used. It starts only if you accept the cookie banner. If you refuse, or make no choice, Google Analytics is not loaded and no Google cookie is saved.

sectionGaBullets.title: Provider
sectionGaBullets.desc: Google Ireland Limited (for people in the European Economic Area and Switzerland) and Google LLC (United States).

sectionGaBullets.title: Purpose
sectionGaBullets.desc: Statistics only: pages viewed, where visitors come from, device type, clicks on external links and downloads. We do not use the data for advertising or to profile you. Google Analytics 4 does not store IP addresses.

sectionGaBullets.title: Legal basis
sectionGaBullets.desc: Your consent (art. 6(1)(a) GDPR; art. 31 nFADP). The choice is free: the site works the same if you refuse.

sectionGaBullets.title: Transfer outside the EU and Switzerland
sectionGaBullets.desc: Data may be transferred to the United States, to Google LLC. Google takes part in the EU-US and Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework; otherwise the standard contractual clauses apply.

sectionGaBullets.title: Retention
sectionGaBullets.desc: Google Analytics cookies (_ga and _ga_…) last at most 2 years. Statistical data in the Google Analytics account is kept for at most 14 months.

sectionGaBullets.title: How to withdraw consent
sectionGaBullets.desc: Click “Cookie preferences” at the bottom of every page and choose “Reject”: Google Analytics stops and the _ga cookies are deleted. You can also delete them from your browser. Your choice is saved only in your browser. Withdrawing does not affect what was collected before.

privacy.section3Title: Section E: your rights (GDPR and nFADP)
privacy.section3Intro: Under articles 15-22 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and articles 25-29 of the Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP):

section3Bullets.title: Access and portability
section3Bullets.desc: The database is in the standard SQLite format: the controller can extract and export the whole archive in an open format at any time.

section3Bullets.title: Correction and deletion
section3Bullets.desc: Every customer or draft quote can be corrected or deleted immediately from the program's interface.

section3Bullets.title: Withdrawing consent
section3Bullets.desc: You can withdraw your consent to Google Analytics at any time from “Cookie preferences” at the bottom of every page.

section3Bullets.title: Storing invoices
section3Bullets.desc: The legally compliant storage of XML e-invoices sent to the Sistema di Interscambio (Italy) is done through the official channels of the Agenzia delle Entrate or through your own accountant.

privacy.section4Title: Section F: contact and how to exercise your rights
privacy.section4Text: To exercise your rights (section E), or for questions about privacy or security, write to the data controller, Davide Nava:

contribute.lead: FatturaFacile grows thanks to people who give it a little time: developers, students, accountants, translators and people who try it. Even a small help counts.

flow.title: From issue to release
flow.lead: The same workflow for every repository. Automated checks (lint, tests and build) run on every pull request.

steps.title: Pick an issue
steps.desc: Start from an open issue (the "good first issue" ones are a good start) or open a new one, and mention it in the Telegram group.

steps.title: Create a branch
steps.desc: Organisation members work on a branch of the repository; everyone else uses a fork.

steps.title: Open a pull request
steps.desc: Against the dev branch (on repositories that have one, otherwise main), with a clear description of what changes and why.

steps.title: Review
steps.desc: At least one approval and green checks are required. After the merge, the changes show up in the development environment.

steps.title: Release
steps.desc: When dev is stable it moves to main; versions are released with a tag (vX.Y.Z).
